mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in PARKS from -32.0 to -4.6, together with still-elevated RESIDENTIAL, signals more discretionary local outings that spill into nearby retail and dining within the next month, pushing RETAIL_REC above its last-4-week mean.
failure_condition: If PARKS rises while RETAIL_REC does not increase over the following 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A further weekly improvement in TRANSIT from around -41 to above -35 indicates commuting recovery broadens access to shopping corridors and lifts retail visits within 1-2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -35 after being below -40
failure_condition: If TRANSIT moves above -35 and RETAIL_REC stays below its prior 4-week average over the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES remains depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays positive, shopping shifts toward neighborhood trips and delivery substitution; this suppresses retail visits over the next four weeks relative to the prior month.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains below baseline and RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, reject the claim.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls by more than 3 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES also weakens, the combined signal implies a tightening mobility environment that reduces retail-and-recreation mobility over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls > 3 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES falls > 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If both proxies drop sharply and RETAIL_REC does not fall within the next 7 days, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM above baseline indicates routine local errands are recovering first, and that foot traffic then diffuses into nearby retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 0 and stays positive for 2 weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays positive for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in PARKS after a brief rebound indicates weather or calendar-driven outdoor substitution has ended, which frees discretionary time for indoor shopping and lifts RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15 after being above -10 in the prior week
failure_condition: If PARKS drops back below -15 but RETAIL_REC remains flat or lower over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and TRANSIT both improve together, the same households that are moving around more convert some of that movement into shopping trips, producing a near-term increase in retail mobility.
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT both rise but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a partial reopening regime, a simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals more daytime circulation in business districts, which should lift retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve together but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean within 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
